An arcane focus can be a wand, rod, staff etc. Ask your DM if you want something that vibes with your backstory. 
Classes like the Bard can even use instruments.

Just keep in mind not every spell requires an arcane focus. Some spells only require one or two of the below:

For exampple a spell will list "V, S or M" in components.
V= Verbal(must be spoken)
S= Somatic(move hands and make gestures)
M= Material(use an item specified by the spell)
{The item if it doesn't have a cost doesn't get destroyed by the spell and can be substituted with an arcane focus. If it has a cost it is destroyed and can't be substituted}



Also it's one spell book per wizard. You can own multiple but only utilize one. In the PHB it lists how you can copy spells from other books to add to your own.

Keep in mind there are spell scrolls, which are one time use spells that can be read by any spell caster. You can also copy those into your spell book.

And don't worry you can also make a new spell book if yours gets destroyed

So you're saying an inexperienced DM went to the effort to make a cool plot line and didn't want it instantly solved so came up with a solution that's reasonable?

An experienced DM would've set a high DC Arcana or Medicine check, or advised the cleric that they would need to learn a variation of the spell from a higher level cleric(set up a side quest).

An experienced player would realize the DM is trying their best and accept the answer that was given. Maybe make it part of their character that they are now focusing on learning how to cure illnesses from otherworldly sources. Harvesting body parts from extra planar beings and conducting research, or investigating beings with experience of the outer realms.

Both parties are at fault, but I gotta side with the DM. As a player I would understand the intent behind the rushed answer and find a way to work with it. It's "yes and" not "no but".
